TelecommandContext.description:
Behavioral layer: telecommand interval analysis.

Captures the execution timing pattern of the command correlated with the
safe-mode entry event.

Phase 3 made ``gap_seconds`` and ``gap_percentile`` optional. They were
required, but presets 4, 5 and 6 ship them as null (the interval statistics
were not computed for those payloads), so ``CrashDumpRequest.model_validate``
rejected three of the ten scenarios the API serves. A missing statistic is
represented as absent rather than as a fabricated number.

anomaly_flag.description: True if the interval crosses baseline bounds
anomaly_flag.title: Anomaly Flag

event_id.description: Unique sequence identifier for the telecommand execution log
event_id.title: Event Id

gap_percentile.description: Historical percentile rating of this execution delta. None when not computed.
gap_percentile.title: Gap Percentile

gap_seconds.description: Delta-T in seconds since the previous execution of this command. None when the interval statistics were not computed.
gap_seconds.title: Gap Seconds

TelecommandContext.title: TelecommandContext

TelemetryEntry.description:
CANONICAL telemetry reading — one channel at one time step.

Phase 3 made this the single representation of a telemetry sample. It is
deliberately SELF-DESCRIBING: everything a detector or a safety check needs
is on the entry, so no consumer has to reach for a parallel legacy array.

Before Phase 3 the bounds lived only on the legacy ``pre_fault_telemetry``
dicts while status and timing lived only on the window entries, which is why
Phase 2 found a scenario reporting zero anomalies when read from the window
alone. ``app/api/adapters.py`` merges both into this shape.

anomalous.description: Source-supplied anomaly flag, when the source provides one. SENTINEL's own verdict lives in the AnomalyReport, not here.
anomalous.title: Anomalous

baseline_mean.description: Observed baseline mean, when the source measured one
baseline_mean.title: Baseline Mean

baseline_std.description: Observed baseline standard deviation, when measured
baseline_std.title: Baseline Std

nominal_max.description: Upper bound of the nominal range
nominal_max.title: Nominal Max

nominal_min.description: Lower bound of the nominal range
nominal_min.title: Nominal Min

parameter.description: Telemetry channel designation, e.g. V_bat, channel_41
parameter.title: Parameter

relative_time_s.description: Parsed offset in seconds; negative is before the event
relative_time_s.title: Relative Time S

status.description: Per-reading status. Defaults to UNKNOWN, never to NOMINAL.

value.description: Numeric reading. None when unusable — see value_text.
value.title: Value

value_text.description: The raw reading when it is not a usable number, e.g. 'NaN' or 'DEGRADED'. Preserved so a NaN stays distinguishable from a missing sample; the old schema coerced both to None.
value_text.title: Value Text

TelemetryEntry.title: TelemetryEntry

TelemetryStatus.description:
Per-reading status label.

Phase 3 widened this from a bare ``str`` validated against three values to a
closed enum covering the labels the repository actually uses. The old
three-value check rejected real data: presets 5 and 6 use WARNING, and the
ESA-ADB dumps use NOMINAL_CONTEXT and LABELLED_ANOMALY, so
``CrashDumpRequest.model_validate`` failed on scenarios 4, 5 and 6.

``normalize()`` accepts the aliases found in the existing data so no stored
payload has to be rewritten.
TelemetryStatus.title: TelemetryStatus

description:
Unified data-intake schema validated by FastAPI before AI processing.

Design goals:
  1. Strict validation for required fields (fault_type, scenario_id).
  2. Backward-compatible: fields added by the new layered schema
     (incident_id, fault_register, telecommand_context,
     pre_fault_telemetry_window) have sensible defaults so the existing
     frontend LOCAL_PRESET_SCENARIOS still pass validation.
  3. Extra keys (hardware_state, operating_context) are silently
     forwarded via ``extra = "allow"`` — the LLM prompt sees them.

event_log.description: Raw event log entries from the spacecraft
event_log.title: Event Log

fault_register.description: Hexadecimal bitmask of HW/SW flags that tripped FDIR
fault_register.title: Fault Register

incident_id.description: Unique alphanumeric identifier for the safe-mode incident case
incident_id.title: Incident Id

pre_fault_telemetry.description: DEPRECATED — superseded by pre_fault_telemetry_window. Accepted on input and merged into the canonical window by app.api.adapters.canonical_window(), which is the only place the two shapes are reconciled. Do not read this field directly: it lacks timing and status, and reading only the window instead cost Phase 2 a scenario that reported zero anomalies because the bounds lived here and nowhere else.
pre_fault_telemetry.title: Pre Fault Telemetry

pre_fault_telemetry_window.description: CANONICAL pre-fault telemetry. All consumers read this field, via app.api.adapters.canonical_window(). Entries are self-describing: timing, value, status, bounds and baseline statistics all live on the entry.
pre_fault_telemetry_window.title: Pre Fault Telemetry Window

safe_mode_trigger.description: Trigger string that caused safe-mode entry
safe_mode_trigger.title: Safe Mode Trigger

scenario_id.description: Scenario identifier used by the demo UI
scenario_id.title: Scenario Id

telecommand_context.description: Behavioral interval log for the correlated command
